basis: Peripheral nerve injury from uremia; kidney failure is the underlying separately diagnosed disease, not damage caused by this neuropathy.

decisions.renal: none: renal failure causes the uremia but is a separate underlying disease; the neuropathy itself damages peripheral nerves.

basis: Anterior uveitis and gangrene each occur in 30-79% per supplied HPO, supporting eye and skin injury. Transient rash excluded; myocarditis and encephalitis occur in 5-29%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: gangrene establishes tissue necrosis, not a separate common vascular lesion; myocarditis occurs in 5-29%.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: gangrene represents destructive tissue injury and is annotated frequent (30-79%); transient rash alone would not qualify.

basis: Skeletal muscle dystrophy with defining eyelid and pharyngeal muscle dysfunction; ptosis 6/6 and dysphagia 3/7. The supplied mapping places the pharynx under pulmonary.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pharyngeal muscle degeneration defines oculopharyngeal dystrophy; the guide explicitly assigns the pharynx to pulmonary.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia reflects defining pharyngeal myopathy, mapped to pulmonary; separate oral, esophageal or intestinal injury is not established.

basis: Scoliosis/contractures 2/2, strabismus 2/2 and sensorineural hearing loss 1/1 support involvement. Respiratory failure alone does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure in 2/2 may arise from neuromuscular dysfunction; direct lung injury is unestablished and aspiration pneumonia is a separate complication.
decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus in 2/2 represents persistent ocular alignment dysfunction; retained alongside skeletal and hearing impairment.

basis: Mesenteric vessel obstruction; qualifying bowel injury is not established in >=30% across this broad concept. Ischemic bowel disease can be separately diagnosed.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: obstruction or stenosis alone does not establish bowel damage; >=30% qualifying injury is unsupported, and ischemic bowel disease is a distinct consequence.

basis: Sterol-biosynthesis disorder with defining cataracts and severe neonatal hepatopathy; global developmental delay is a defining neurologic feature, retained within the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay is a defining feature; retained here because metabolic mechanism, cataracts and hepatopathy fill the three primary slots.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this syndrome is an established CYP51A1-related sterol-biosynthesis disorder, so the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Corticospinal degeneration defines SPG8. Peroneal atrophy and pes cavus occur in 30-79% but reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than direct muscle or bone disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent peroneal atrophy and pes cavus are secondary to neurologic dysfunction; direct skeletal myopathy or bone disease is not established.

basis: Defining skin and oral mucosal erosions; oral abnormalities and enamel hypoplasia occur in 80-99%. Structural airway abnormalities occur in 5-29%; stridor alone is insufficient.

decisions.pulmonary: none: stridor and hoarseness are symptoms; documented laryngeal stenosis and upper respiratory tract abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: mucosal blistering is part of the definition, with characteristic oral erosions and enamel defects; mouth and teeth map to gastrointestinal.

basis: Neurodevelopmental syndrome historically named for microphthalmia; ocular malformations occur in 30-79%. Scoliosis and hypodontia each occur in 80-99%.

decisions.ocular: primary: microphthalmia is a defining feature in the historical syndrome name; microphthalmia and iris coloboma are annotated in 30-79%.

basis: Mitochondrial disorder with defining cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy (1/2); pulmonary hypoplasia 2/2. Neurologic involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the definition explicitly locates respiratory-chain deficiency in skeletal muscle and describes characteristic weakness; biopsy-supported myopathy occurs in 1/2.
